page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the N4 server family. It is equipped with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical Intel x86_64 core with hyperthreading enabled (2 threads per core) and dedicated CPU resource allocation. The instance features 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Its Intel processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, along with hardware support for vector and matrix instruction extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance includes no attached local NVMe storage and no discrete GPUs.

Single-threaded benchmark evaluations show average compute efficiency, indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1834.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1684.29. However, due to its single physical core constraint, multi-core throughput drops significantly into lower percentiles, as evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 2251.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2984.94. Uncached memory bandwidth is limited, achieving 19.35 GB/sec for reads and 12.78 GB/sec for writes on 256 MB test blocks. Workloads involving heavy parallel compute, multi-threaded software compilation, or high-throughput memory operations experience notable scaling limitations.

From a resource density perspective, the n4-standard-2 provides entry-level access for lightweight general-purpose applications requiring dedicated CPU cores rather than burstable credit models. The addition of advanced Intel instruction sets like AMX and AVX-512 enables small matrix or cryptographic processing tasks despite low overall core counts. Ideal deployment profiles include lightweight web applications, simple background microservices, low-traffic API endpoints, basic text processing, and developmental staging environments that do not require high concurrent memory or multi-core compute throughput.
